no65.summary: The French envoys at Ferrara to François I on their audience with Alfonso I d'Este, duke of Ferrara, after the reverence to Madama Renée and Don Ercole: the duke refuses to take the kingdom of Naples for himself or the captaincy of the French army, offers only to accept whatever accord the King negotiates for him with the Pope, and pleads the want of provisions; the agents judge his difficulties pretexts and fall back on Ercole and on Trivulzio. arya/ct/read_no65_duke_answer.md is Patel's separate reading of the Duke's answer (f. 119v) with Lasry's key, controlled on the clear twin no. 66.
no65.en:
Last Thursday I, Gian Joachino, arrived here and went straight to the lodging of the ambassador messer Gaspar Sormano,
where I am; and having communicated to him Your Majesty's intention and commission, and shown him its instruction and
mandate, and having discussed at length between us and settled the way to proceed with this ◎, so that a conclusion
might be reached according to Your Majesty's desire: having paid our respects to Madame Renée and to the lord Don
Ercole, we were with the said ◎, and having presented Your Majesty's letters of credence with such fitting words as
seemed fitting to us, we set out our credence, and in Your Majesty's name we persuaded, encouraged, and earnestly
exhorted and begged His Lordship to be willing to accept what he, as his good and affectionate son, should ferisse(?)
and resolve:

no66.summary: The independently drafted duplicate of no. 65, which writes in clear many of the passages no. 65 enciphers and the reverse, so that the pair cribs each other; it opens with Gian Gioacchino de Passano's arrival at the lodging of the ambassador Gaspare Sormano. arya/ct/clear_texts.md holds Patel's transcription of the clear passages of nos. 63, 65, 66 and 67.
no66.en:
Last Thursday I, Joachim, arrived here and went straight to the lodging of the ambassador Messer Gaspar Sormano,
where I am now staying. I told him Your Majesty's intention and commission and showed him the instruction and
mandate, and between us we discussed at length and settled how to proceed with the [Duke] so that a conclusion might
be reached as Your Majesty desires. After paying our respects to Madame Renée and Lord Don Ercole, we went to the
aforesaid [Duke]. We presented Your Majesty's letters of credence with fitting words and set out our credence, and
in Your Majesty's name we persuaded, encouraged, earnestly exhorted and begged His Excellency to accept what Your
Majesty, as his good and affectionate kinsman, was offering him, and to resolve to accept it: to undertake the
enterprise of Naples on the terms and conditions in the instruction.

no63.summary: The follow-up to the duplicate pair of 23 February, the most heavily enciphered of the three; its third sheet f. 123r, bound out of order and dated 'penultimo de Febraro', ends the letter on Naples and the captaincy, and its postscript reports from Rome that the Pope has relapsed, 'sensa speransa di salute', and that the French cardinals should make ready for a conclave.
